historical_references.time_period: The period of the Umayyad Caliphate (661-750 AD)
historical_references.context: Rukham ibn Zuhayr was an Arab poet from the tribe of Khamas. He was known for his panegyric poetry, particularly the praise he lavished on Umayyad caliphs. In the time of Al-Walid I, Rukham wrote a famous poem known as 'Al-Mu'allaqat' (The Suspended) that he hoped would hang in the Kaaba alongside other great poems.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Al-Jamahiriyah Al-Khayrniyah by Al-Maqrizi, Volume 1, Page 307 The name Rukham carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.time_period: The period of the Mamluk Sultanate (1250-1517 AD)
historical_references.context: Rukham al-Ansari was a prominent Islamic scholar, theologian, and jurist during the Mamluk period. He was also a prolific author, contributing significantly to various fields of Islamic studies. Rukham is best known for his commentary on Imam Malik's 'Muwatta', which became a standard reference work in Sunan jurisprudence.
